I did laminate floating floors: On the concrete part you have to have a vapor barrier. I got big-assed plastic sheets from the painting section at Wally Mart and taped then down with orange painter's tape (that shit holds pretty good). My planks came with a 12mil foam backing thus I did not need any additional padding / squeak protection. The floor is relatively soft to walk on which I like. We are old.

The stairs where far and away the hardest part of the install. I did them with the same laminate. Managed to burn up my prized Milwaukee reciprocating saw prepping the treads. Take you time on stairs and remember that it's the front edge of the tread that gets the most weight pit on it. So that part has to be supported by the facia unless you do solid wood treads. We pulled up all the baseboards and corner trim pieces and undercut the door jambs with an oscillating saw. Broke a few baseboards along the way but the extra effort really shows up in the finished work once the trim was reinstalled.

Why clinical trials are seeking minority volunteers

Vaccines and medicines can work differently in different racial and ethnic groups, so diversity in clinical trials is important.
